successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Picenum, 'all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo', except Ancona and Asculum

ledger.x: c. 500 BC: the Picentes 'in the area between the Foglia and Aterno rivers'; 'Picenum including all of today's Marche and the northern part of Abruzzo'; they 'had no predominant inhabited centre, and therefore had no need for a capital'. No formation date; 500 is a placeholder before the treaty of 299. The page's…
299 BC: 'When in 299 BC the Romans captured Nequinum, they also concluded a treaty with the Picentes'; the Picentes become allies of Rome, tinted from roman-republic (vassal_start picentes 299).
269-268 BC: 'The Picene revolt against Rome began in 269 BC, the "Picentine war"'; the consuls Appius Claudius Russus and Publius Sempronius Sophus sent against them.
269 BC: the Picentes 'broke the alliance and in 269 BC revolted and started the Picentine war' (roman-republic /ledger/29 ends the tie in 268, with the annexation).

268 BC: 'Rome then annexed the rest of Picenum, except Ancona and Asculum, which kept allied status'; civitas sine suffragio 268, 'civitas optimo iure' 241; part of the population deported to the Silarus (Picentia) and Lake Fucino; Firmum 264.
268 BC: annexation; Ancona and Asculum allied cities (the roman-republic dossier's vassal_end note).

wars.name: Picentine war
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Picenum annexed except Ancona and Asculum

certainty.note: The Marche and northern Abruzzo between the Foglia and the Aterno.
